text:
maya: Heads-up — after swapping the canary gating metric from BLEU->embedding-sim we started seeing a subtle degradation for int8-quantized v2 on the chat benchmark. Not obvious in latency but user-facing quality downpaths. Posting quick snapshot.

samir: which benchmark / metric window? numbers?

maya: 10k chat queries sampled, emb-sim avg dropped from 0.87 -> 0.81 for int8 v2 vs float baseline 0.89. BLEU stayed ~flat which is why it slipped past the old gate.

li: interesting — sounds like metric mismatch. emb-sim is more semantics-focused but can be noisy for short replies. Do we have example failures?

maya: pasted a few diff excerpts:
- baseline float: "Sure, you can schedule that for Monday." -> good
- int8 v2: "I think so? Possibly Monday?" -> conversational but more hedging, lower embedding sim.

olivia: rollout-bot just opened an automated alert: "canary-metric-window: warning: emb-sim drop 0.06 over 1h; fail_count=4" :warning: 

rollout-bot: CanaryProgressReport: deployment=int8-v2 canary_traffic=10% metric=embedding_similarity window=60m drop=0.06 threshold=0.03 -> ACTION=auto-pause

ben: we should not rely on single metric for auto-fallback. propose dual gating: require emb-sim AND a task-specific token-accuracy proxy or pairwise human-sim. Also add hysteresis for tiny drops.

samir: agree. propose simple rule set: 1) canary traffic 10% 2) require emb-sim delta <= 0.03 AND quality-regression-rate <= 1.5x baseline over 3 consecutive windows 3) auto-fallback only after 3 window failures. quick config snippet:

```
canary:
  traffic: 0.10
  metrics:
    - name: embedding_similarity
      max_delta: 0.03
    - name: short_reply_regression_rate
      max_ratio: 1.5
  failure_windows: 3
  auto_fallback: true
```

li: also add a prompt stratification check — short vs long queries. emb-sim collapse mostly on <10 token replies.

maya: OK I'll rollback the current canary to float immediately and update gating logic. Can we add an eval job to run 50k stratified queries overnight? :coffee:

olivia: noted — scheduling eval job. tagging @data-team for human spot-checks.

ben: long-term: we should maintain a small metric suite per workload and surface per-prompt skews in the console. For now: rollback + dual-gate + 3-window auto-fallback.

maya: thanks all — will follow up with PR for gating config and results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
